founder_decisions_applied.F1: cost line only; no effect on this table
founder_decisions_applied.F2: seals may appear on unchecked islands with an unchecked-content label; changes M3. Nothing in this table depends on whether an island is checked (see R-SEAL-UNCHECKED)
founder_decisions_applied.F3: M1 is built on a branch and released only when checks are green; no effect on this table
founder_decisions_applied.F4: no holdout; no effect on this table

fixture_island.note: a three-lesson fixture island, in this island order; it is not Number Island

how_to_read.time: Every time is milliseconds elapsed since the history's t0 (UTC instant), which is real elapsed time. Local calendar days never matter; tz is given only for the three rows whose point is that they do not.
how_to_read.step: Steps are applied in order. now_ms is the moment the learner's screen is read after the step. event.at_ms is when the record was made; it can be earlier than now_ms (late arrival). After each step the expectation is read at now_ms.
how_to_read.expect: states (per lesson: not-started | explored | understood | unknown), counts (null whenever the store is unknown, never zero), another_look (lessons showing the worth-another-look cue). due, next and seal_attempt appear only on steps that assert them. Multi-device histories give by_device.

events.recall: {lesson, at_ms, correct, source, qv}; source is scheduled | seal | practice | replay | research_probe | qa_shortened | null (pre-M1); a null source comes with a null qv
events.recall_skipped: recall shown and skipped or abandoned, no option chosen
events.flag_practice: a flag practice session; its answers are recall records with source practice
events.qv_change: the lesson's current recall question version becomes qv
events.open_world: learner opens the World; open, select_option, predict, dwell, scroll: engagement only
events.choose: learner explicitly picks a lesson; read in that step only
events.store_status: the progress store becomes ready | blocked | unreadable (records, if given, are what a ready store then holds); ownership_change: account ownership checking or switching
events.sync: the listed devices push to the account and pull the merge, in the order listed; account_seed: rows already in the account before any device

how_to_read.legacy_writer_proof: false unless engineering has shown, in the M1 record, that the due-revisit path was the only writer of recalls before M1 (3.2 rule 6, P1.7).

rulings_needed.question: When engineering's proof exists, does a pre-M1 recall (null source, null qv) match the lesson's current question version? The table says yes (it counts as scheduled).
After a sync, is the first recorded reveal the earliest across devices? The table says yes.
rulings_needed.if_no: the last step becomes E on both devices

rulings_needed.question: Brief 3.3 says the seal opens when every lesson is Explored. The table reads that as: has a recorded reveal, so an Understood lesson counts. (Otherwise the seal branch of 3.4 is reachable only while some lesson is Explored and, by 24 hours, due.)
rulings_needed.if_no: the seal rows must be redrawn

rulings_needed.question: EDD-018 section 3 adds that all sampled questions must be due; brief 3.3 lists four conditions and not that one. The table follows the brief. Under the EDD reading, a due lesson wins branch 2 of 3.4, so branch 4 would never be reached.
rulings_needed.if_no: head-of-product to say which text governs before the build

rulings_needed.question: Under F2 a seal may open on an unchecked island. The table never sets an island's checked state and asserts nothing that depends on it; M3's table must.

other_reading_choices: A cue (worth another look) exists only while the latest qualifying answer is wrong. A wrong answer that does not qualify (under 24 h, practice, old version) gives no cue.
A question version change retires every older answer for that lesson, wrong ones included: the state is Explored with no cue until a new-version answer.
Due is asserted only where the schedule is unambiguous: not answered at all and 1 day or more since the first reveal, or answered once and still before day 3, or answered once and long overdue.
A source of seal is written only for an eligible seal attempt. An ineligible attempt is recorded as practice.
Records are ordered by at_ms; two records at the same instant are not tested.
An explicit choice applies only in the step where it is made.

histories.title: A fresh learner with a readable, empty store starts at stop 1 and sees real zeros
Opens, selections, predictions, scrolling and dwell never leave Not started
A recorded reveal is Explored; all three revealed and nothing else gives optional practice
86,399,999 ms after the first reveal does not qualify
86,400,000 ms after the first reveal qualifies
A recall on the next local calendar date but 1 hour later does not qualify (America/New_York)
Across the autumn clock change, 24 h elapsed qualifies although the wall clock moved 23 h (America/New_York)
Across the spring clock change, 24 wall-clock hours is only 23 h elapsed and does not qualify (America/New_York)
A replay reveal does not move the anchor: the gap runs from the first reveal
A recall dated before the lesson was ever revealed is ignored, even after the reveal arrives
covers: EDD-018 section 3: ignore recalls without a completion

histories.title: A recall for a lesson with no recorded reveal leaves it Not started
covers: EDD-018 section 3: ignore recalls without a completion

histories.title: Flag practice answers, however correct and however late, never make a lesson Understood
A wrong answer in practice changes nothing for an Understood lesson
Replay, research-probe and QA shortened-day answers, though correct and late, do not make Understood
Wrong answers from replay, probe and QA shortened days do not reset an Understood lesson
A correct answer inside an eligible seal attempt qualifies like a scheduled one, only for a revealed lesson
Only the latest qualifying answer for a lesson decides, scheduled or seal
A scheduled and a seal answer for one lesson within 24 hours count once
An answer to an older question version does not count; the current version does
A changed question sends an Understood lesson back to Explored, with no wrong-answer cue, until a new-version answer
covers: time/edits do not claim a wrong answer

histories.title: After a version change an old wrong answer no longer decides the state or the cue
A later qualifying wrong answer returns an Understood lesson to Explored with a cue; a later correct one restores Understood
A first qualifying answer that is wrong leaves Explored with a cue; a later correct one gives Understood
A wrong answer 86,399,999 ms after the first reveal gives no cue; at 86,400,000 ms it does
After a qualifying wrong answer, a correct practice answer leaves Explored and the cue; time does not clear it
A skipped or abandoned recall neither qualifies nor resets anything
After 400 days Understood, Explored and Not started are unchanged; due is a separate mark
A lesson becomes due while staying Explored, and is no longer due once answered
Recalls with null source and null qv leave the lesson Explored when engineering has not shown the due-revisit path was the only writer
With engineering's proof recorded, null-source null-qv recalls count as scheduled ones
New-format records decide; an old-format record, even a later-dated one from an old client, does not change the state
A blocked store shows no state, no count and only the fixed Start-here marker; when it opens, real states appear
An unreadable store is Unknown, never zero; once readable and empty it is a true fresh record
Until account ownership settles every lesson is Unknown, and no count is shown
A store that stops being readable turns every lesson Unknown, not Not started; recovery restores the real states
Switching account clears the visible states at once (no leak of the old account), then shows the new account
covers: EDD-018 section 4: clear on account switch

histories.title: A recall answered on device A reaches device B with the same source and qv, and both show the same state
A wrong on A and a later correct on B settle to Understood on both, whichever device syncs first
A correct on A and a later wrong on B settle to Explored with the cue on both
Account rows written before the migration (null source, null qv) give Explored on both devices; a new row then gives Understood on both with its fields intact
covers: account rows before the M1 migration

histories.title: After sync the first reveal is the earliest across devices, so the 24 h gap runs from it
Syncing the same records twice changes nothing and counts the answer once
Records are ordered by their timestamp, not by arrival: an older correct answer arriving late does not undo a newer wrong one
The same recall delivered twice is one answer
An answer for one lesson never changes another lesson, and practice on a third changes nothing
A lesson the learner explicitly chose is the suggestion, over a due revisit and over the first unexplored stop
A due revisit beats the first unexplored stop, and several due revisits go in island order, not in the order they became due
The first unexplored stop is the earliest one in island order, not the one after the last visited
With every lesson explored, the seal attempt is suggested only once 86,400,000 ms have passed since the last first exploration
After a flag practice the seal attempt is closed until 86,400,000 ms later
